newsitem.title: GERMANY: VDA says June a strong month for German carmakers.
newsitem.headline: VDA says June a strong month for German carmakers.

text.p: German vehicle production, driven by fresh demand for exports, showed double-digit growth in June but failed to offset slow months at the start of 1997. Six-month output rose a mere three percent, the VDA German vehicle association said on Friday.
The VDA said domestic production in June totalled 470,300 vehicles, up 16 percent over June 1996, while exports rose 18 percent to 281,700.
The monthly report also reflected fresh demand in Germany as estimated new registrations rose nine percent to 367,700 vehicles.

But six-month figures reflected tough times for German carmakers. Total production compared with the 1996 period rose only three percent to 2.60 million vehicles during the first six half of 1997 and new vehicle registrations fell two percent to 1.99 million.
The VDA said passenger car production rose 15 percent in June to 440,000 units, exports were up 17 percent to 261,700 and new registrations were up eight percent to 342,000.
On a six-month basis, passenger car production rose two percent to 2.43 million units, exports were up seven percent at 1.45 million but registrations fell three percent to 1.85 million.

The report also noted strong demand for trucks weighing up to six tonnes. Six-month production rose 13 percent to 105,000 units, exports were up 14 percent at 69,400 units and new vehicle registrations rose seven percent to 95,000.
